answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every identity to post a refundable work bond before it may transact. Like a mesa that stands only because its base is solid rock, an agent's standing rests on locked stake: the bond returns only after peers attest a run of honest tasks. A newcomer starts in a small garden plot of low-value jobs; good work lets its reputation grow, while a failed attestation forges a public slash of the bond. Spawning ten thousand fake agents means locking ten thousand bonds, so the attack costs real capital instead of free keystrokes.
